anomalies.observed: R17, the series current-limit resistor for indicator LED5 (yellow), is labelled 330k on the FCC sheet. Every other indicator LED on the FCC and NAVC sheets uses a 100 or 330 ohm resistor (R15 330, R16 330, R18-R20 100, and NAVC R33-R36 330/100).
anomalies.expected: A 330 ohm series resistor, matching the other yellow indicator LED (LED11/R35 330 on the NAVC sheet) and the ~3 mA indicator design used across the board.

anomalies.impact: At 330k the LED draws only a few microamps, so the yellow indicator will be effectively dark. This removes a status indication from the FCC without affecting flight-control functions.

parsed.summary: The FCC indicator-LED network has a current-limit resistor R17 valued at 330k, about three orders of magnitude above the 330 ohm used for the matching yellow LED on the NAVC sheet and for the other LED channels. The rest of the reviewed power, sensing, and interface connections look consistent with the specification.
